title: Early Contributor Activation: 10/30/90 Craft Kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, practical kit for activating engineers and product-adjacent hires in their first 10 / 30 / 90 days. Focus is on fast, measurable impact plus the evidence managers need to make early success decisions. This is intentionally streamlined for small teams and remote hires; use as-is or adapt to role-specific templates.

Audience:
- Hiring managers (first point of contact)
- Onboarding mentors and buddies
- People Ops partners and hiring panel leads
- New hires (as their personal activation checklist)

How to use this doc:
- Copy into a candidate-specific onboarding doc in the manager's folder.
- Add links to role-specific repos / runbooks and a short 30-min kickoff calendar invite.
- Fill the "evidence" items during interviews and first-week checkpoints so manager decisions are async-friendly.

10-day (week 0–2): immediate setup and signal tasks
- Day 0: welcome thread, laptop & infra checklist completed (IT ticket reference), 30-min intro with manager scheduled.
- Access: GitHub, internal docs, Slack, CI, dev infra, staging creds verified. Document any missing items and escalate within 24 hrs.
- Quick win assignment (<=2 days): small, scoped PR that exercises the dev/testing loop (example: fix a flaky test, add small doc, add a short unit test).
- Buddy pairing: assigned buddy should do daily 30-min pairing sessions for first 5 working days.
- First-week 1:1 with manager: expectations, immediate priorities, and psychological safety check.
- Evidence capture: new hire adds a short journal entry after each pairing session (bullet notes). Manager tracks completion.

30-day (end of month 1): breadth, ownership, and interview evidence validation
- Ownership task: take end-to-end ownership of a small slice (feature flag flip, minor routing change, dashboard tweak). Deliverables: design note, implementation PR, and rollout checklist.
- Cross-team intro: 15-min syncs with 2 adjacent stakeholders (product, infra, or SRE).
- Metrics baseline: capture relevant metric(s) (latency, error rate, throughput, NDAs) and write a 1-paragraph hypothesis about where to improve.
- Interview evidence rubric (manager and panel): capture signals in the following simple format for each candidate/hire:
  - Technical craft (code quality, testing, architecture sense): observed examples (2 bullets)
  - Problem decomposition (how they structure work): observed examples (2 bullets)
  - Communication & collaboration (async clarity, PR notes, cross-team asks): observed examples (2 bullets)
  - Learning velocity (how quickly they picked up infra/concepts): observed examples (2 bullets)
  - Risk flags (onboarding blockers, access gaps, role fit questions): short notes
- 30-day review: manager and buddy sign-off on whether hire is on-track / needs remediation / should be re-scoped. Keep notes in the candidate doc.

90-day (end of month 3): consolidation and scaling expectations
- Lead-level deliverable: propose and implement a non-trivial improvement that touches reliability, performance, or developer experience; include rollout plan and rollback criteria.
- Mentorship: begin mentoring a new hire or contract, run a brown-bag knowledge share.
- Career conversation: manager runs a growth & expectation conversation; document next skills to build and a 90-day stretch plan.
- Performance evidence pack (3 artifacts): link to PR(s), a short postmortem or design doc, and metrics showing change.
- Decision: manager recommends one of: keep (on-track), extend onboarding (30d), or role pivot/closure. Document rationale in 3 bullets.

Interview rubric & evidence guidance (for panel leads who later own onboarding):
- Keep it micro: each panelist contributes 2–3 concrete evidence bullets. Avoid long narratives.
- Evidence vs opinion: attach the artifact where possible (PR, note, recording). Example: "Fixed token cache bug — changed LRU policy and added unit test (PR #1234)".
- Confidence score (0–3) as a single number next to evidence: 0=no evidence, 1=weak, 2=solid, 3=strong. Use to synthesize.

Manager / Mentor commitments (template to paste into calendar invite)
- Manager commits: weekly 1:1s (30 min) for first 90 days, weekly async updates in manager doc, provide prioritized list of 3 objectives for first 30 days.
- Mentor commits: 5×30min live pairing sessions in first 2 weeks, code review turnaround <48 hours, help unblock infra issues within 24 hours.
- Buddy responsibilities: daily quick check-ins week 1, run a short retrospective at day 10 capturing blockers/answers.

Quick manager triage checklist (use at 10 and 30 days)
- Access problems still open? (yes/no) — if yes, escalate to IT with ticket id.
- PR/assignment completed? (yes/no) — if no, identify missing dependencies.
- Social syncs scheduled? (yes/no) — if no, schedule two 15-min intros.
- Evidence log populated? (yes/no) — if no, request panel notes.

Common onboarding blockers and remedies
- Missing infra access: escalate + provide temporary mocked env with clear steps.
- Over-scoped first tasks: break into two sub-tasks and reassign quick wins.
- Isolation from product context: short product deep-dive session and one-pager summary.

Notes-to-self / open questions for people-ops:
- Should we standardize the quick-win PR examples per role? (y/n)
- How to pair internal promo calibration with this evidence pack — propose a lightweight template for L4->L5.
- Do engineering leads want a 15-minute "handoff checklist" for managers when closing a loop on an offboarded buddy?

Next steps / owner map
- People Ops: publish a templated Google Doc from this kit and add to the onboarding starter (owner: Asha).
- Engineering managers: adopt for every new hire and attach evidence in candidate doc (owner: hiring manager).
- Mentors: confirm buddy roster in the team channel before offer acceptance (owner: team lead).

Appendix: example checklist to copy into a candidate doc
- Day 0: laptop & access checklist completed (ticket #)
- Day 1–5: 5 pairing sessions scheduled and 2 executed
- Day 3: quick-win PR created (link)
- Day 14: ownership task scoped and kickoff done
- Day 30: 30-day review note and evidence bullets
- Day 90: 90-day deliverables linked and recommendation recorded

Contributors: Diego (template tweaks), Nina (mentor ops), Samir (metrics baseline examples).

End of doc.
